blocks.text: It is the opposite process of pair production. For example, when an electron and a positron interact to each other they annihilate into two gamma ray photons as shown in Fig. 12.4. The reaction can be written as

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book cites Fig. 12.4 here, but the annihilation of an electron and a positron is Figure 12.2; Fig. 12.4 shows the three radioactive radiations.

The energy of each gamma ray photon is 0.51 MeV which is equal to the rest mass energy of an electron or a positron, i.e. E = m₀c². In an annihilation reaction energy and momentum are conserved. Besides the electron and positron annihilation, the annihilation reactions of other particles and their anti-particles can also be carried out e.g., proton and antiproton, lepton and antilepton, quark and antiquark, etc.

blocks.alt: A wavy photon labelled hν travels along a straight arrow to a nucleus drawn as a cluster of nucleons. From the nucleus a positron (+e, kinetic energy K₊) leaves upward and an electron (-e, kinetic energy K₋) leaves downward, each at an angle θ to a dashed line that continues the photon's path.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.1: A high energetic photon interacting with a nucleus and disappears into an electron and a positron pairs (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.1).
blocks.long_description: The photon comes from the left. The positron is a green ball on the upper path and the electron a grey ball on the lower path; the arrows at the ends are marked K₊ and K₋, and the two equal angles θ are measured from the dashed line.

blocks.alt: A horizontal line with an electron e⁻ on the left and a positron e⁺ on the right. At the centre a vertical wavy line crosses it, with arrows showing one gamma ray going up and one going down.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.2: Fusion of electron and positron (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.2).

blocks.text: High energy collisions between the particles at CERN have revealed that some mass of colliding particles is changed to electromagnetic radiation according to Einstein's equation and left over mass appears in the form of new sub-atomic particles.
